name: Hot Medium Roast Coffee
description: Mild and flavourful.

name: Shimmi's Preferred Hot Coffee
description: Lots of depth from the dark roast, balanced well with the medium hazelnut coffee. Finished well with the sweeted and flavour of the cinnamon bark.
notes: More hazelnut coffee, less dark roast. Only a hit of cinnamon or it will be overwhelming.

name: Pure Hazelnut Flavoured Coffee
description: Medium roast with the hazelnut flavouring is smooth and balanced.

name: Blended Hot Brew Coffee
description: More complex than plain hazelnut coffee.

name: Blended Cold Brew Coffee
description: Coarse grounds, cold water, 12–18 hours. Remarkably smooth and low-acid. Perfect summer drink.
notes:
Tried and amazing.
Tastes "weaker" than hot brew due to different compound extraction, not actual strength -> caffeine content is high.
Best made in a glass jar in the fridge overnight.

name: Pure Dark Roast Coffee
description: Strong and bold, a bit acidic.
notes:
Bit too strong for my liking. 
Used Woolworth Kenyan Dark Roast.

name: Simple Hot Mint Tea
description:
Clean and delicate, slightly grassy.
Fresh mint leaves steeped in hot water.
notes: The mintiness does not come through. Almost taste cooked.

name: Mint + Lemon Water
description: Clean and refreshing.

name: Hot Peppermint Tea
description: Soothing and warming hot.

name: Hot Peppermint + Citrus Tea
description: Soothing and warming hot.
notes: Grapefruit slice adds a nice floral citrus brightness.

name: Hot Hibiscus Tea
description: Tart and deep red, juice-like quality.
notes:
Quite nice, a bit tart — feels like a juice.
Good to add honey as well.

name: Hot Hibiscus + Citrus Tea
description:
Tart and deep red, juice-like quality.
Citrus add more freshness to it.
notes:
Too much citrus made it a bit overwhelming. Use in moderation.
Good to add honey as well.

name: Hot Hibiscus + Naartjie Tea
description:
Tart and deep red, juice-like quality.
Citrus add more freshness to it.
notes:
Dried naartjie great in moderation.
Good to add honey as well.

name: Plain rooibos tea.
description: Classic rooibos tea.
notes: Tried flavoured varieties (likely peach, cherry cranberry) — both unremarkable. Plain rooibos is the winner, flavoured versions not worth seeking out.

name: Ice Medium Roast Coffee
description: Smooth and flavourful

name: Cold Mint Water
description: More interesting to drink than plain water.

name: Mint + Lemon Water
description: Hot water classic.

name: Citrus Rooibos Tea
description: Extra citrus freshness that does well with the rooibos

name: Naartjie Rooibos Tea
description: Extra naartjie freshness that does well with the rooibos

name: Rooibos Honeybush Blend
description: Very high quality, adds extra flavour.

name: Rooibos Chamomile Blend
description: Soothing and delicious. Good for sleeping

name: Ginger rooibos tea
description: Extra kick from ginger.
notes: I personally don't enjoy it.

name: Classic Korean Barley Tea
description: Roasted and nutty.

name: Toasted Naartjie Barley Tea
description: Dried toasted naartjie peel adds a layer of fruitiness to it whilst upping the savouriness of the tea.

name: Citrus Barley Tea
description: Pomelo zest adds a nice citrus kick and freshness which cuts well with the toasty flavour of the barley

name: Shimmi's GI Remedy
description: Soothing for the stomach and very delicious.
notes: Steeping overnight brings out the flavours even more.

name: Hot Ginger Water
description:
Works on it own. Sharp, soothing and warming.
Good for GI issues, nausea and stomach discomfort.
notes: But better paired with other ingredients.

name: Ginger Jujube Water
description: Jujube adds a bit of sweetness to the sharp ginger taste. Very delicious and soothes the stomach.
notes:
Add more ginger for more sharpness!
Some people might find it strong.

name: Hot Perfume Water
description: Tastes like perfume.
notes: Lemongrass too overpowering. However, could try with more moderation.

name: 红枣水
description: Sweet and mellow. Bit boring on its own.
notes: Better as a supporting ingredient.

name: Hot Cinnamon Water
description: Warming and slightly sweet. Woody and comforting. Surprisingly good!
notes:
Slight astringent notes left behind. 
Tastes sweet due to cinnamaldehyde, not sugar. 
Apparently helps with blood sugar or something?

name: Cinnamon Naartjie Blend
description: A pleasant warming drink with a slow reveal — the naartjie citrus comes forward first, bright and aromatic, before the cinnamon gradually kicks in with its characteristic sweetness and earthiness. The dried naartjie peel rounds everything out with a soft, warm citrus quality rather than a sharp acidic hit. Comforting and layered.
notes:
Naartjie dominates initially — citrus oils volatile and hit the palate first, cinnamon takes a while to come through.
Cinnamon still detectable underneath, adding sweetness and earthiness once it kicks in.
Previous attempt was a second steep so not a fair test — this is the proper version.
For next try: reduce naartjie peel slightly (2-3 small pieces) and steep cinnamon 5-10 minutes first before adding naartjie — goal is cinnamon forward with naartjie as a warm background hint rather than the star.

name: Zimbabwean CBD Blend
description:
Ingredients:
CBD flower, silver needle (白毫银针), star anise, cloves, black and white peppercorn, rose.

A warming, aromatic wellness blend. Spiced like a gentler chai with floral softness from the rose and silver needle. The CBD adds a relaxing quality without being heavy.
notes:
Dad got this for me while he was in Zimbabwe. I don't know why he got this, but I don't think he read the label and just though it was a cool tea...

Go easy on steep time initially as the cloves and peppercorn can become overwhelming.

name: Glühwein
description: Classic German mulled wine. Warm, spiced and deeply seasonal — perfect for a cold Joburg winter weekend. Spices continue developing in the flask over time.
notes: Fortified with a few extra shots for good measure.

name: Hot Water
description: Plain ol' hot water.
notes: Don't drink it too fast!

name: Cold water
description: Wow it's cold!

name: Hot Water (stove)
description: Now, why don't you own a kettle?

name: Cardamom Coffee
description: Tastes good, but would be better with milk.
notes: Quite nice but would work better as a milky coffee — cardamom latte style.

name: Hazelnut cloves coffee
description: Flavour profile: hazelnut brings sweet nutty warmth as the base, cloves add deep almost numbing spiced intensity on top. Rich and complex, the cloves give the hazelnut an unexpected edge. Not a gentle cup — more like a statement coffee.
notes: Not my favourite

name: Cinnamon cardamom water
description: Sweet and spiced
notes: Nice but not too interesting — possibly didn't get the ratio right. 1 cinnamon stick to 2–3 cracked cardamom pods recommended. Cinnamon should dominate, cardamom as the accent. Worth retrying.

name: Cinnamon Rooibos
description: Enjoyed a lot. Tastes cosy and almost dessert-like — like a spiced biscuit or a chai-lite without the astringency. The rooibos softens the cinnamon so it's warming but not sharp. Sweet, warm and very easy to drink.

name: Pseudo "Ginger Beer"
description: Tastes almost like a warm, light, natural ginger beer — spicy from the ginger, sweet and woody from the cinnamon, none of the artificiality of actual ginger beer. A really satisfying combo.

name: Jujube Rooibos Honeybush Blend
description: Unlogged — try it and repoThe natural mellow sweetness of jujube blends beautifully with the honeybush's floral sweetness. Soft, naturally sweet and comforting with a gentle fruity depth underneath.rt back

name: Chamomile
description: Lovely. Gentle and soothing with a natural apple-like sweetness. Very easy to drink.

name: Rose petal tea
description: Quite nice. Light and floral but not overwhelming. Colour can range from yellow/golden to pale pink depending on rose variety and water pH — adding a squeeze of lemon shifts it towards pink. A subtle, elegant drink — more perfumed hot water than a punchy tea, in the best way.

name: Floral Cinnamon Blend
description: Pretty good but ratios need tweaking. Too little cinnamon — woody notes came through without the sweetness.
notes: Chamomile and rose balance well together. Next try: increase cinnamon slightly to about half a stick to bring out the sweetness. Promising combo.

name: Warm Mojito
description: Very delicious. The cool, bright intensity of peppermint and the fresh citrus sharpness of lemon complement each other beautifully — each lifting the other without either overpowering. Clean, refreshing and zesty. A very natural pairing.

name: Spiced Fruit Punch Tea
description: Deep tart ruby-red base from the hibiscus, warm spiced sweetness from the cinnamon softening the tartness, fragrant mandarin citrus brightness from the naartjie peel lifting the whole thing. Tastes like a warm spiced fruit punch — almost like a non-alcoholic mulled wine. Deeply aromatic and festive.

name: Hibiscus Ginger Tea
description: Two strong flavours fighting rather than complementing. Tastes quite herbal. Tart and sharp upfront from the hibiscus, ginger heat building underneath, no sweetness to bridge them.
notes: More functional wellness drink than enjoyable sip. Would need honey or jujube to mediate between the two.

name: Ginger peppermint tea
description: Tastes strongly herbal, both too assertive and neither complementing the other. Similar issue to hibiscus + ginger.
notes: Not an enjoyable drink — two strong flavours clashing.  Functional for GI issues but not a pairing worth drinking for pleasure. Avoid for casual brewing.

name: 云南红茶
description: A robust, full-bodied Yunnan black tea with natural honey and cocoa sweetness. One of the more forgiving black teas for longer steeping due to its bold character.
notes: Amazing on a short steep — phenomenal. Unsure how it holds up on a longer steep, tannins may turn it astringent. Stick to shorter steeps for now and test longer steeps cautiously.

name: 菊花茶
description: Always had it at Chinese restaurants. Very light, delicate and naturally sweet — subtle rather than pronounced. Clean and refreshing with a gentle floral quality. Easy to drink, nothing assertive. Good on its own.

name: 陈皮红枣
description: Really enjoyed. Light, refreshing and naturally sweet. Great period day combo — refreshing without being heavy.

name: 红枣大麦茶
description: Note: Good but not amazing. Soothing and smooth but not too interesting on its own. Better as part of the three-way blend with ginger where the ginger adds the lift it needs.

name: Lemongrass Water
description: Nice — citrusy and kinda floral.

name: 米汤
description: Light, refreshing and surprisingly tasty.

name: Ronnefeldt Rooibos Cream Orange
description: Ingredients: Rooibos, orange peel, vanilla
notes: Mom's favourite. Full-bodied rooibos with creamy vanilla and ripe orange notes. Lovely.

name: Ronnefeldt Green Angel
description: Ingredients: Green tea, natural pear and peach flavouring
notes: Mom's favourite. Gentle green tea with a slightly tangy note and sweet juicy pear and peach flavour. Lovely. One of Ronnefeldt's most popular teas.

name: Hot apple cider
description: Delicious

name: Chamomile Lemon Tea
description: Good. Like normal chamomile but with an extra citrus kick to it. Bright and refreshing without losing the gentle soothing quality of chamomile.

name: Cinnamon Hazelnut Coffee
description: Good as expected. Hazelnut's natural sweetness and cinnamon's warmth are a natural fit.

name: Peppermint naartjie tea
description: Peppermint too assertive early on, overpowering the naartjie. Steeping longer brings out the naartjie but weakens the peppermint. Both ingredients on opposite steep curves — never quite at full strength simultaneously.
notes: Nice but tricky to get right. Pleasant but not the bright peppermint + citrus combo expected. Fresh lemon slice works better with peppermint as it releases more immediately.

name: Cinnamon Dark Roast Coffee
description: Good. Bold and earthy from the dark roast with warm sweetness from the cinnamon. A natural pairing.

name: Spiced naartjie dark roast coffee
description: A bold and layered coffee drink. The dark roast provides the earthy, robust base while the dried naartjie peel adds a surprising creaminess and softness — rounding out the edges of the dark roast rather than adding sharp citrus. The cinnamon weaves in depth and spice underneath, adding warmth without overwhelming. Together it's a citrusy, spiced dark roast with more complexity than the sum of its parts.
notes:
Quite good overall. Added slightly too much cinnamon which tipped it too sweet — dial back the cinnamon next time.
The naartjie peel's role here is softening and rounding rather than dominating, which works really well with coffee.
Worth retrying with less cinnamon to find the right balance.

name: Pure cardamom tea
description: Floral, aromatic and warming. Quite light initially but develops significantly with a long steep — the oils in the pods need time to fully release, especially if the seeds inside aren't fully exposed.
notes:
Used 6 small pods, cracked open.
Light and pleasant at 15–20 minutes — quite floral and aromatic but subtle.
Strengthens considerably after a full afternoon steep — stronger cardamom taste, quite nice and enjoyable.
Recommend long steep for best results. Crack pods aggressively and expose the seeds for better extraction.
May lose potency if pods are old.

name: Cold Peppermint Tea
description: Clean, light and refreshing — a more subtle version of hot peppermint tea. The menthol comes through gently without the intensity of a hot steep. Almost like a natural mint water.
notes:
Alright but quite light — not as punchy as hot peppermint.
Flavour improves and develops nicely as it steeps throughout the day — gets progressively better rather than staying static.
Drank throughout the day rather than overnight — flavour develops gradually as it steeps.
Remove teabag after 8 hours to avoid bitterness.
Best as a light refreshing drink rather than a flavour-forward one.

name: Cold Brew Hibiscus Tea
description: Light and refreshing, tart and cranberry juice-like but quite mild compared to hot hibiscus. Colour extracts but flavour stays relatively subtle even after overnight steeping.
notes:
After 1 hour — very light, watered down cranberry juice character.
After overnight steep — slightly stronger but not by much. Doesn't intensify dramatically with more time.
Teabag likely less efficient for cold brew than loose hibiscus — bag material restricts passive cold water diffusion.
Worth trying loose hibiscus petals cold brewed for comparison — may extract significantly better.

name: Cold steeped rose petal tea
description: Delicately floral and softly sweet — even more subtle and clean than the hot steep version. Almost like a floral water, very gentle and elegant. The cold extraction pulls the colour out into a striking purplish-pink, while preserving the delicate aromatic quality of the petals.
notes:
Floral and lovely.
Colour correction from hot steep entry: cold steep produces a purplish-pink colour, hot steep produces yellow. Cold water extracts the anthocyanin pigments more gently without heat degrading them.
Use a generous amount of petals since cold extraction is less efficient than hot.
Steep overnight for best results.

name: 盗版酸梅汤
description: Short steep produces a sweeter, slightly spiced hibiscus tea — the cinnamon adds warmth and sweetness without dramatically changing the character. Overnight steep transforms it into something much more complex — vaguely reminiscent of 酸梅汤, the tartness of hibiscus and warm spiced depth of cinnamon merging into a layered, almost nostalgic drink.
notes:
Loose hibiscus tastes about the same as teabag — no meaningful difference.
Short steep: sweeter hibiscus with a cinnamon hint.
Overnight steep: the real version — deeper, more complex, 酸梅汤 vibes.
Steeping all night and day can be very strong — dilute slightly with water for a more pleasant drink, especially when cooled.
Recommend overnight steep, slightly diluted and cooled for best results.

name: Cold brewed dried pomelo skin
description: Bitter and citrusy — sharp and cleansing rather than comforting or sweet. A mood-based drink rather than an everyday one. Works well as a palate cleanser.
notes:
Used quite a few pieces — likely too many, contributed to the bitterness.
Bitterness comes from pith still attached to the skin, unlike naartjie zest which is pith-free.
Use fewer pieces next time to reduce bitterness.
Worth trying paired with 红枣 or honey to balance, or barley tea as a base which softened it well previously.
Best when you want something sharp and cleansing rather than something sweet or comforting.

name: Turmeric hot steep
description: Warm, earthy and grounding. Gently bitter with a clean, pure turmeric flavour — slightly medicinal but in a comforting, wholesome way rather than unpleasant. Fairly soothing. Water turns a warm golden yellow.
notes:
Method: first steeped in hot water previously (flavour partially depleted), then sliced and re-steeped in hot water for a few hours.
Next proper test: cold soak overnight first to rehydrate without losing flavour, then slice and hot steep for a fuller extraction.
Pairs well with ginger and cinnamon to balance the bitterness.

name: 茉莉花茶
description: A delicately scented green or white tea base infused with fresh jasmine blossoms. Floral and fragrant with a naturally sweet, perfumed quality — the jasmine aroma is soft and lingering rather than sharp or overpowering. Light and clean on the palate, with a gentle warmth that makes it equally pleasant hot or cold brewed.

name: Hot steeped naartjie peel
description: Warm and fragrant citrus — softer and rounder than the cold version, with an upped creaminess from the heat. Less bright and citrusy than cold brew, but the sweetness is similar. Gentle and comforting rather than sharp.

name: Cold brew naartjie peel
description: Clean and light citrus — cold extraction pulls the fragrant oils gently without the warm cooked-orange quality you get hot. Refreshing and subtle.
notes: Nice and clean. Drinking throughout the day rather than overnight — gets stronger as the day goes on, which works well. Use more peel than you think you need.

name: Naartjie chamomile tea
description: Gentle and comforting — chamomile's apple-like sweetness with soft citrus warmth from the naartjie. Naartjie comes forward first then softens into the chamomile base.
notes: Quite nice, as expected. A natural pairing — both ingredients are round and gentle so they don't compete.

name: Acid Test
description: Testing
